expert_proposals.title: Withdraw statistics_target escalation; test planner cost recalibration instead
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: default_statistics_target=300 was accepted on a single lucky replicate (30.4% gain) while the second replicate gained only 0.52%; the frozen p50/p95 decrease predictions were refuted in both blocks, so finer histograms are not the lever. GetUserTweets still consumes 88% of terminal capacity at p50=175us with an Index Scan plan, so the residual cost is per-call index descent and heap fetch, not selectivity estimation.
expert_proposals.mechanism: The r006 statistics escalation is withdrawn: it produced no reproducible latency reduction and its mechanism verdict is refuted. The dominant GetUserTweets path is already an Index Scan at estimated cost 8.45 with estimated_rows=1, so the remaining per-call cost is index descent plus heap tuple visibility checks. Lowering random_page_cost from 1.5 to 1.1 and seq_page_cost from 0.8 to 0.7 keeps the planner firmly on the index path while making the cost model consistent with a fully cached working set (2TB RAM, shared_buffers=512MB, zero io_waiting_backends), which prevents any marginal plan flip to a seq scan on skewed user_id values and stabilizes the hot path's per-call cost.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets retains its Index Scan plan; the cost model no longer over-penalizes the cached random index descent, so no plan flip to sequential scan occurs on skewed user_id predicates and per-call latency stays at or below the incumbent p50.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Neutral-to-slightly-positive: stabilizing the dominant transaction's plan removes variance-driven tail stalls; expected +0.3% to +1.0% successful TPS, not a large jump.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 unchanged or marginally lower; p95 unchanged within noise. No regression expected on InsertTweet.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from 1.5 to 1.1 within safe [1.0,6.0]; measured zero io_waiting_backends and 2TB RAM mean random index reads are cache-resident, so cost should approach seq_page_cost.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of cached random index descent on the hot GetUserTweets path

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from 0.8 to 0.7 within safe [0.5,2.0]; keeps the random/seq ratio near 1.57 so the index path stays preferred without over-penalizing cached heap fetches.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost to preserve index-path preference

Stabilizing the 88%-capacity transaction frees terminal time for additional completions.

alternatives.statement: default_statistics_target is already past its useful plateau at 300; further increases add ANALYZE cost with no plan change because the hot query is a single-row index lookup.
The residual GetUserTweets cost is commit-path WAL sync (sync_average_ms 0.137, wal_waiting_backends max 1), so only the WAL commit-path bundle can move TPS; planner cost knobs will be neutral.

cross_domain_requirements: WAL commit-path bundle (commit_delay/commit_siblings/wal_writer_flush_after) remains the memory_storage nomination; planner cost change is orthogonal and additive.

expert_proposals.title: WAL commit-path bundle: widen group-commit window and writer flush batch
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 and wal_writer_flush_after=0 leaves the WAL writer flushing per-write; wal_waiting_backends persists at max=1 and sync_average_ms=0.137ms across both replicates, so commit-path syncs are not being coalesced.
expert_proposals.mechanism: WAL sync latency and wal_wait are present but small (sync_average_ms 0.137ms, write 0.026ms, host_io stalls 0). The commit path is not the dominant bottleneck (GetUserTweets terminal_capacity_fraction=0.88), yet the mandatory wal_commit_path bundle is actionable. Widen the group-commit collection window (commit_delay 100->500us) and lower the activation threshold (commit_siblings 2->3) so 5 terminals' commits coalesce, and set wal_writer_flush_after 0->256 (2MB) so the writer batches flushes instead of flushing per write. wal_compression stays on (already enabled, non-actionable). This tests whether coalescing syncs reduces wal_waiting_backends and sync time without adding per-commit stall.
expert_proposals.query_effect: No plan change expected; commit-path coalescing affects InsertTweet commit latency and WAL wait, not GetUserTweets index path.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (0.3-1%) if WAL wait is on the critical path for InsertTweet commits; otherwise neutral.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 may decrease slightly; GetUserTweets unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 500us within safe [0,1000]; 5x window to collect 5 terminals' commits, still under 1ms added latency.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings reliably triggers group commit without over-gating.
Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units) within safe [0,1024]; 2MB flush batch reduces writer sync frequency versus per-write flushing.

predictions.rationale: Wider group-commit window plus 2MB writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs, lowering average sync time.
Fewer per-commit syncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity for completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: WAL wait is incidental; GetUserTweets terminal saturation dominates and TPS stays flat regardless of commit-path tuning.
Widening commit_delay adds fixed per-commit stall that outweighs coalescing, lowering InsertTweet throughput.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Targets the persistent wal_wait anomaly with a coherent group-commit + writer-flush-batch action while leaving the accepted default_statistics_target=300 and cache settings intact; bounded amplitude keeps added commit latency under 1ms.

nodes.label: WAL commit-path bundle: commit_delay 500, commit_siblings 3, wal_writer_flush_after 256
Wider group-commit window plus larger writer flush batch coalesce fsyncs

expert_proposals.title: Reverse falsified predicate-lock coarsening: tighten max_pred_locks_per_page/relation
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: max_pred_locks_per_page=2 and max_pred_locks_per_relation=-2 (defaults) were raised in r005/r006 to coarsen SIRead locking; r005 was refuted and r006 remains parked. The SERIALIZABLE retry regime is inactive (server_retry_ratio=0.0, rollback_ratio=0.0, lock_waiting_backends.max=0.0), so predicate-lock promotion is not the binding constraint; the falsified direction should be reversed to the tightest safe granularity to test whether finer SIRead locking reduces per-txn lock bookkeeping (locks_total.p95) without harming GetUserTweets tail.
expert_proposals.mechanism: r005 raised max_pred_locks_per_page 2->8 and max_pred_locks_per_relation -2->4 and was refuted on TPS. r006 proposed a larger amplitude (32/16) but is untested. With zero server retries, zero rollbacks and zero lock waits, SIRead promotion is not causing serialization aborts; the coarsening direction is unsupported. Reversing to the safe low bounds (page=0, relation=0) forces the coarsest page/relation-level SIRead granularity, minimizing per-tuple predicate-lock bookkeeping and locks_total. This is a bounded direction reversal of a falsified group, not a replay.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets (87.99% terminal capacity) predicate-lock bookkeeping per call should shrink; no plan change expected.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (>=0.3%) if lock bookkeeping is on the critical path; unchanged if terminal saturation dominates.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 should not regress; locks_total.p95 should decrease.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; reversal of falsified 2->8 (r005) and untested 2->32 (r006).
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 0 forces coarsest page-level SIRead locking

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0; reversal of falsified -2->4 (r005) and untested -2->16 (r006).
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 0 forces coarsest relation-level SIRead locking

predictions.rationale: Coarsest page/relation SIRead granularity reduces per-txn predicate-lock entries.
Less lock bookkeeping shortens the dominant transaction's tail.
Freed terminal capacity from GetUserTweets raises completed TPS.
No lock waits observed; granularity change should not create waits.

alternatives.statement: If GetUserTweets is purely terminal-bound, locks_total.p95 falls but TPS stays flat; then the bottleneck is client-side, not predicate locks.
If coarser SIRead granularity increases false conflicts, lock_waiting_backends.max rises above 0.
